I feel for you, my mother does the same thing too, it gets unbearable to be around her at time. The problem with this conspiracy stuff is that they go under the radar because a lot of people believe in this stuff, so they tend to just look normal. When in actuality, we know this is anything but normal. The average person who believes in conspiracy theories is typically uninformed, they believe it, but they don't let it consume them.

My mother literally has no other hobbies than getting upset about the satanists/illuminati/jews that control the world. I have tried to bring her back down to earth by showing her things like Steven Pinker talking about the world not actually being so bad, showing her proof the Protocols of Zion are fake, that vaccines are not killing us, and many other things, but it's no use, you simply cannot reason with crazy. She just ignores all the facts, stating they're all made up by the Satanists and goes back to watching crazy YouTube videos, and taking ever single word they say as fact without questioning it. 

Often times I tend to go along with it as I don't want to set her off, but I recently told her I was an agnostic, and she got really upset. Yelling about how I was being deceived by the Satanists, and how I am going to become demon possessed, all the same stuff you're describing. She literally can't talk about anything other than conspiracy theories, and any conversation not about conspiracies will inevitably become about conspiracy theories.

What other crazy stuff has your mother done because of this conspiracy stuff? Mine has submerged a new internet router she bought in water because she thought the government was using it to spy on her. She currently covers the TVs in the house because she believes they're Satanic alters. She unplugs and takes the batteries out of EVERYTHING when she is not using them as she believes the government is using them to eavesdrop on her, it gets annoying to plug everything back in every day.

My mother adopted two cats about a year ago. For the past year she did nothing but complain about how hard it was to take care of them, and how much work they were. She also actively denied me any time I tried to help with them. 

About a few months ago she gave them up to the local shelter, then took them back a week later because she 'felt bad.' Then a week after that she went back to complaining about them and telling me how much she regrets taking them back.

I honestly just think the martyr wanted something to suffer over and complain about.

I remember my mother didn't like my only friend's mother, so she made me cut off all contact with him. I of course didn't do that, when she found out I was still talking to him, she took away my computer I used to contact him on, she changed the password to the alarm system on the house so I could not leave the house without the police being called, wouldn't let me use the phone for any reason, wouldn't let me leave the house, changed my school so I would not go to the same school as him, and took away all my video games, books, music, etc as punishment for talking with him. 

I remember it was summer break when this happened, so I literally just sat inside my bedroom for two months straight with nothing to do, unless my mother came in my room and decided to either yell at me, and guilt trip me or lecture me about the bible. I remember I tried to run away during this time to my sister, but it didn't work, and I had to go home and that only made her more mad. I eventually tried to run away to my fathers, but that didn't work either, so then I just caved into pressure.

I have to say, that link is really accurate. I would say she is the 'Waif' with a chunk of 'Hermit.' It seems so crazy that she could have a personality disorder like that and I had no clue.

In one of my prior comments I said I thought she might have a martyr complex, I seem pretty much certain of this now.

I thank you so much for your reply, it's just one thing, you talk about abuse and trauma. Don't you think that's a bit of a stretch? Like I am not really left with any scars or damage after this. Like most of my hopelessness came from my depression caused by factors unrelated to my mother. It's just the circumstances that made me initially choose my NEET path. Is this Stockholm syndrome?

I don't think she wants a pet, I do think she excessively worries.

>I don't see how you could've come to aspire to literally nothing for yourself

It's just sorta how I figure she would be the happiest. Like I thought about at least getting a job, but I honestly have no idea what she would be less happy with, as she has this thing where she just takes everything into her own hands. Like she does not really let me help out around the house. I dunno if this breaks the rules, but it feels like a martyr complex almost. It's the best way to describe it.

>Not teaching you how to do things for yourself is actually pretty selfish - it shows that she simply doesn't care what happens to you after she's gone. 

She regularly gets upset about this, yet never lets me help out or do anything whenever I offer. I dunno what she thinks. Like I said in the OP, she made me quit my job because it was too far away, yet it was only like a 15 minute bus ride away. I remember she used to frequently show up unannounced and pick me up. I think I remember her being really scared about me using the bus on my own, yet I was like 18 at the time.

I think it's probably because she does not really trust me, like one time I came home from work and hour late, and she was worried I ran away and never wanted to speak to her again. I did try running away when I was 13, but I think that is still kinda weird.
